description: Reacts to loud sounds by startling, blinking, or crying
flag_message: Your baby doesn't seem to react to loud sounds yet. This is worth mentioning at your next visit — it's one of the earliest signs of hearing we look for.
slp_notes: Check hearing first before assuming language delay

description: Turns head or eyes toward familiar voices and sounds
flag_message: Most babies turn toward familiar voices by 4 months. If your baby isn't doing this, let your pediatrician know — a hearing check is a good first step.

description: Turns or looks when their name is called
flag_message: Responding to name by 9 months is an important social-communication milestone. If this isn't happening consistently yet, mention it at the 12-month visit.
slp_notes: Also a key autism screen item (M-CHAT)

description: Pauses or looks up when told 'no'
flag_message: Understanding simple words like 'no' usually happens around 9–12 months. Keep tracking — if it's not emerging by 15 months, bring it up with your pediatrician.

description: Follows simple instructions like 'give me the ball' without you pointing
flag_message: Following simple directions (without pointing) by 18 months is a key language milestone. If this isn't happening, an early speech-language evaluation can help identify any support needed.

milestone_name: Points to body parts when named
description: Points to eyes, nose, ears when asked
flag_message: Most children can point to at least 1–2 body parts by 18 months. If this isn't emerging, it's worth tracking carefully through the 2-year visit.

description: Follows two-step directions like 'pick up the cup and give it to me'
flag_message: Understanding two-step directions by 24 months is expected. If this is difficult, a speech-language evaluation is recommended.

description: Produces vowel sounds like 'ooh' and 'aah'
flag_message: Most babies start cooing by 2–3 months. If your baby isn't making any vowel sounds yet, it's worth noting at the next checkup.

description: Produces a clear laugh
flag_message: Laughing usually emerges around 4 months. If your baby isn't laughing or vocalizing socially, let your pediatrician know.

description: Babbles with consonant sounds like 'ba', 'ma', 'da'
flag_message: Babbling with consonant sounds should be emerging by 6–7 months. No babbling by 9 months is a red flag for both hearing and speech development — request a hearing test if not already done.
slp_notes: No babbling by 9 months = refer for hearing eval + SLP

description: Uses 1–2 words meaningfully (beyond 'mama' and 'dada' as labels)
flag_message: Most children say their first word by 12 months. If no meaningful words have appeared by 16 months, an early speech evaluation is recommended — earlier is always better.

description: Says 'mama' or 'dada' referring to the correct parent
flag_message: Using 'mama' and 'dada' as real labels (not just sounds) usually happens by 12 months. If this isn't happening by 15 months, mention it at the next visit.

description: Has a vocabulary of at least 10 words
flag_message: A vocabulary of at least 10 words by 18 months is a key milestone. If your child has fewer than 10 words, a speech-language evaluation is recommended. Research shows early support leads to significantly better outcomes.
slp_notes: This is a primary EI referral trigger

description: Has a vocabulary of at least 50 words
flag_message: 50 words by 24 months is a well-established milestone. If vocabulary is significantly below this, a speech-language evaluation is important.

description: Combines two words together (e.g. 'more milk' 'daddy go')
flag_message: Combining two words by 24 months is expected. If your child isn't doing this yet, a speech evaluation is the right next step.

description: Uses three-word phrases regularly
flag_message: Three-word phrases typically emerge between 24–36 months. If language is notably less complex than this by age 3, mention it to your pediatrician.

description: Smiles in response to familiar faces and voices
flag_message: A social smile (smiling back at you) usually appears by 2 months. If your baby isn't smiling responsively by 3 months, it's worth bringing up at the next visit.

description: Makes and holds eye contact during interactions
flag_message: Good eye contact is foundational for communication development. If your baby rarely makes eye contact by 3–4 months, mention it at the next checkup.
slp_notes: Key autism screening item — handle messaging carefully

description: Takes 'turns' vocalizing — you talk, baby responds with sounds
flag_message: Back-and-forth sound exchanges (the early version of conversation) should be emerging by 4–6 months. If your baby doesn't engage in vocal back-and-forth, note it for the 6-month visit.

description: Looks where you're pointing to see what you're showing them
flag_message: Following a point to see what someone is showing you (called joint attention) is a critical early communication skill. If this isn't happening by 12–14 months, a developmental evaluation is recommended.
slp_notes: Major autism screening item — be careful with wording

description: Points at things to share them with you (not just to request)
flag_message: Pointing to share interest ('look at that!') is one of the most important early social-communication skills. If this isn't happening by 14–16 months, a developmental evaluation is recommended.
slp_notes: M-CHAT item — autism screening relevance; avoid alarming language

description: Waves goodbye when someone is leaving
flag_message: Spontaneous waving (not just when prompted every time) typically emerges by 12 months. If your child isn't waving yet, note it for the 12-month visit.

description: Copies simple actions and sounds you make
flag_message: Imitating actions and sounds is how babies learn — it's also a key social-communication milestone. If imitation is absent by 15 months, mention it at the next visit.

description: Uses objects symbolically in play (feeds doll, talks on toy phone)
flag_message: Simple pretend play typically starts around 18–24 months. If play is still very concrete and repetitive by 30 months, it's worth discussing with your pediatrician.

milestone_name: Variety of consonant sounds in babble
description: Uses a range of consonant sounds (b m p d g k)
flag_message: A variety of consonant sounds in babble should be emerging by 6–8 months. Limited consonant variety by 10 months is worth noting.

milestone_name: Words mostly understood by familiar listeners
description: Primary caregivers understand most of what child says
flag_message: Parents and familiar people should understand most of what a 2-year-old says. If speech is frequently unclear even to you, a speech evaluation is helpful.

milestone_name: Words mostly understood by unfamiliar listeners
description: Strangers can understand most of what child says
flag_message: By age 3, most of what a child says should be understandable to unfamiliar listeners. If speech is hard for others to understand, a speech-language evaluation is recommended.
